kind: G0 functional probe (raw libtorrent, synthetic swarm); not a gate measurement, selects no default

stall_last.doc: stalled peers connected 1 s after the serving ones

watchdog.doc: probe-side detector: requests outstanding and no payload for 2 s -> ip_filter that address

interpretation.reading: Medians [min-max] over the runs of one variant and cell. 'edges' = per run max(piece 0, last piece): with today's start (edges + upstream, gsp02-v4 PASS:C2) playback waits for both boundary pieces. Times from the first connect_peer; harness-bound absolute values, only within-batch differences matter. n=5 for U1-U4/L2 variants, n=3 for U5-U8.
stable_facts: Stalled peers cost the start on today's default path: upstream/mixed edges time 16 MiB 11.82 s [11.22-12.30] with two silent stalled peers vs 4.78 s [4.78-6.83] without (+7.0 s); 4 MiB 5.76 [5.15-9.58] vs 2.40 [2.37-2.41]; 1 MiB 4.41 [3.66-5.47] vs 1.80 [1.79-1.83]. Keep-alive ('chatty') stalled peers behave the same (16 MiB 12.86, 4 MiB 6.43, 1 MiB 4.33).
Where the cost lands depends on the piece: at 1 and 4 MiB piece 0 is unaffected (1.8 / 2.4 s everywhere) and the last piece absorbs the stall; at 16 MiB both (product p0 9.41, last 11.82).

libtorrent 2.1.1 snubs a stalled peer exactly piece_timeout (2/3/5/10 s, the setting) after its first request; request_timeout 2/5 likewise snubs at 2/5 s. The snub only frees the stuck blocks; it does not get them re-requested quickly.

A shorter piece_timeout does NOT improve the start, it moves the delay: 16 MiB piece_t2 p0 5.65 s (from 9.41) but last 13.34 s, edges 13.34 [13.23-15.50] vs product 11.82; piece_t3 14.02, piece_t5 12.81; 4 MiB piece_t2 5.31, piece_t3 6.71, piece_t5 5.55 vs product 5.76. Same with chatty peers (piece_t2_chatty 16 MiB 14.50) and on the legacy start (L2: edges 10.79 / 11.05 / 10.30 for 2/3/5 s). Combining it with request_queue_time 1 does not help either (16 MiB 12.39 / 13.25).

The probe-side watchdog (requests outstanding and no payload progress for 2 s -> ip_filter that address) removes most of the cost: 16 MiB edges 6.34 s [6.30-7.62] (p0 5.69, last 6.34), 4 MiB 4.05 [4.04-4.11]; chatty peers the same (6.35 / 4.05). Bans at 3.55 s (first request 1.52 s + 2 s + 0.25 s sampling). Ranges do not overlap with the product's (n=3).

No false positive in any variant: serving-peer snubs 0 and serving-peer block time-outs 0 everywhere; the watchdog banned 12 addresses, all stalled (0 false); without stalled peers (ctrl_watchdog) 0 bans and times equal to ctrl (16 MiB 4.81, 4 MiB 2.39).
hints_n_small: Stalled peers connecting 1 s after the serving ones (stall_last, n=3, no watchdog): 16 MiB piece 0 at 20.80 s [20.79-20.94], the worst case seen; the watchdog was not run in this order.
peer_timeout 5 helps only silent peers (16 MiB edges 9.16 s); a peer that sends keep-alives is never idle, so it is not a candidate.

Harmful settings (n=3): max_out_request_queue 8 (4 MiB last 12.79 s), request_queue_time 1 alone (4 MiB last 11.23 s), piece_extent_affinity off (16 MiB 13.65 s); strict_end_game_mode on: no change (12.00 s).
not_covered_by_the_probe: A live but high-latency peer whose first block takes more than 2 s (RTT/queueing): the swarm's slowest serving peer here is 0.5 MB/s with 100 ms latency, so the 2 s rule never fired on it.
Several real peers behind one NAT address: an IP ban removes all of them.
A banned peer gets no upload from us either for the ban time (120 s proposed); negligible on a private tracker, but a behaviour change.
Peers that recover after a pause (e.g. disk stall) and the effect of re-admitting them after the ban.
Seek: the probe measures the start only.
interpretation.decision: The stream-scoped piece_timeout candidate is withdrawn (no start improvement on today's path, worse at 16 MiB). The watchdog is the only variant that shortens the start without a false ban; it becomes the SP10 candidate behind a switch (default off) for GSP10.
